Title: Nexa Lighthouse: Transition to Scale funding for climate and health innovation in Asia and the Pacific
Programme: Nexa Lighthouse (climate and health innovation, Asia and the Pacific)
Purpose: Funds proven innovations that help local health actors turn climate-risk signals into timely action, for hazards including extreme heat.
Why (Common Shade's reading): Extreme heat is one of the hazards named in the call.
Who can apply: Applicants incorporated and implementing in countries across Asia and the Pacific; the full list of eligible countries is in Appendix B of the funding opportunity.
Lead applicant location: Incorporated in an eligible country in Asia or the Pacific.
Where the work can happen: Projects implemented in eligible countries in Asia and the Pacific, listed in Appendix B of the funding opportunity.

Title: Open call: share traditional and cultural heat management practices (Southeast Asia)
Issuing organisation: Global Heat Health Information Network (GHHIN) Southeast Asia Hub
Purpose: Community members, practitioners and knowledge-holders are invited to contribute traditional and cultural heat management practices (traditional medicine, vernacular architecture, farming, clothing, oral history) to a public repository.
Why (Common Shade's reading): Heat prevention and management practices are the subject of the call.

Title: IKI Small Grants: eighth call
Purpose: Local climate and biodiversity projects by non-profit organisations in ODA-eligible countries.
Why (Common Shade's reading): A local adaptation project could address heat; fit with the call's themes needs confirming.
Who can apply: Sub-national, national and regional non-profit organisations in ODA-eligible countries.

Title: Horizon Europe: integrating climate-related exposures into the human exposome (HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-ENVHLTH-02)
Programme: Horizon Europe Cluster 1: Health (environment and health topics)
Purpose: Research on climate-related exposures and how the human exposome changes with climate change.
Heat relevance: Related remit with a clear heat application
Why (Common Shade's reading): Heat is a climate-related exposure; the topic is about the exposome broadly.
Who can apply: Consortia; international cooperation is encouraged. Whether a partner from a given Asian country receives EU funding depends on Horizon Europe's country list.
Where the work can happen: Not limited to Europe for participation; funding of non-European partners depends on the country list.

Title: GCF Readiness support: proposals accepted at any time, recommended by 31 March 2027
Purpose: Readiness support for national institutions, country programming and direct access entities; submissions may be made at any time during the Readiness Strategy 2024 to 2027.
Heat relevance: Related remit with a clear heat application
Why (Common Shade's reading): Readiness can support adaptation planning that covers heat, where national priorities include it.
Who can apply: National Designated Authorities, or entities they nominate; not open to other organisations directly.
Where the work can happen: Developing countries that are Parties to the UNFCCC.
Deadline wording: recommended proposal submission date of no later than 31 March 2027

Title: Beat the Heat in Cities: expression of interest for countries and cities

Title: ILO request for quotation: desk review and evidence mapping of occupational exposure to excessive heat in Thailand
Purpose: Desk review and evidence mapping of occupational exposure to excessive heat and its impacts on workers' safety and health in Thailand.
Why (Common Shade's reading): Occupational heat exposure is the subject.

Title: IKI Medium Grants 2026
Purpose: Climate action and biodiversity projects in ODA-eligible countries, led by organisations based in Germany with local partners.
Why (Common Shade's reading): Adaptation has been a theme in past rounds; a heat project's fit depends on the 2026 funding announcement's priorities.
